node.label: Homi K. Bhabha
node.date_label: “Of Mimicry and Man: The Ambivalence of Colonial Discourse” (1984) · Nation and Narration: edited collection (1990) · The Location of Culture (1994) · Stierstorfer interview on diaspora and home (2013)
node.description: Examines cultural difference through contradiction, translation and the processes that produce minorities. In his interview with Klaus Stierstorfer, cultures do not form seamless wholes: their unequal, discordant relations help make theoretical problems visible. He distinguishes specific practices and trajectories from fixed cultural identity. His later discussion of home and refugee status resists treating all mobility as the same endless nomadism; choices, losses, legal positions and different time scales matter. These claims use his own interview answers rather than turning the earlier publisher description of hybridity and mimicry into a fresh chapter reading.

proposed_edges.relationship: Treats cultural translation and minoritization as processes within discordant cultures rather than relations among seamless cultural wholes.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Complete substantive publisher-posted interview read; opening answers on cultural misfit and translation distinguish Bhabha’s statements from interviewer labels. Parsi historical examples remain his situated testimony, not an essential culture or universal minority model.

proposed_edges.relationship: Questions permanent models of belonging through the unequal temporalities and legal conditions of diaspora and refugee life.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own answers on home, narrative choices and final citizenship/refugee section. His ethical proposal to rethink belonging through refugee impermanence remains an attributed proposal; interview does not show all migrants living an identical condition.
